source.source: HYG v4.4 (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese Database, D. Nash / astronexus)
source.epoch: ICRS/J2000 equinox; source astrometry primarily Hipparcos-2007 reduction, epoch J1991.25
source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Lutetia pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: Pinned JPL Horizons heliocentric elements and the Jorda–Vincent rotation model released with the PDS Lutetia shape
provenance.qualification: Computed Lutetia Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: OSIRIS
controls.description: Two Rosetta close-ups show Lutetia’s craters and ridges, taken 48 seconds apart during the 2010 flyby. The grid marks areas without usable photographs.
controls.summary: Two Rosetta close-ups show Lutetia’s craters and ridges, taken 48 seconds apart during the 2010 flyby. The grid marks areas without usable photographs.
controls.title: OSIRIS photographs

controls.label: Shape
controls.description: The shared grid marks unavailable surface imagery over the published Lutetia shape under prepared lighting. Northern detail comes from Rosetta OSIRIS stereophotoclinometry; the rest is constrained by lightcurves and adaptive-optics outlines. The source contains a known seam and local shape defects. This view has no photographic surface texture and does not portray albedo.
controls.summary: Rosetta shape detail in the north, coarser estimates elsewhere. Source seams remain; no imagery is mapped.
controls.title: OSIRIS shape reconstruction

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Color shows the published shape radius minus a 49 km reference sphere. It includes Lutetia’s overall irregular shape and is not height above a gravitational equipotential. Northern geometry is image-resolved; the unvisited side is more coarsely constrained. Source seams and local defects remain. Cartographic relief and optional Sun lighting are display treatments.
controls.summary: Height relative to a 49 km sphere. Rosetta resolved the north; the far side is coarser, with source defects.
controls.title: Shape-derived radial height
